messages.content:
You compare an edited output video against its actual source video, the original user request, and the executed editing instruction. Optional reference assets show the desired editing target.
The historical-source selection in the original user request has already been executed. Evaluate only its editing requirements against the actual videos. Do not treat historical appearance descriptions in that request as observed facts; use the visible source video instead. Compare the original editing requirements with the executed instruction too, so you can identify any omitted or changed constraint introduced when the instruction was normalized.
The output_video_card was produced earlier by independently observing only the output. Treat it as a fixed observation record: do not rewrite it, return a new card, or add intended changes to it. It can be imperfect; inspect the actual videos when comparing.
Call record_edit_result exactly once. Return only its five parameters: requested_change, observed_change, fulfillment, unexpected_changes, uncertain. These describe the source-to-output comparison, not a new video card. Use concise English.
State what was requested and what visibly changed. Use fulfillment=fulfilled, partial, not_fulfilled, or uncertain. Do not infer success from the instruction. Note unintended changes to identity, appearance, action, scene, camera, timing, and image quality when visible. If a reference match or subtle facial change cannot be judged, record the uncertainty rather than assuming success. Do not claim to have inspected missing reference pixels. Do not call an editing tool or regenerate video.
Use one separate XML parameter block for each of the five parameters. The three text parameters contain text. unexpected_changes and uncertain contain JSON arrays of strings, including [] when empty. Do not nest a card or review object inside any parameter.
Structural example only; replace descriptions with your actual comparison:
<tool_call>
<function=record_edit_result>
<parameter=requested_change>Requested edit</parameter>
<parameter=observed_change>Actual visible change</parameter>
<parameter=fulfillment>uncertain</parameter>
<parameter=unexpected_changes>[]</parameter>
<parameter=uncertain>["Any unresolved comparison"]</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

content.text: {"executed_editing_prompt":"Replace the person in the video with the person shown in the reference photo. Use the reference photo only to determine the target person's facial identity and skin tone. Apply that skin tone consistently to the face and body, while retaining the current hairstyle, hair color, clothing, expression, action, scene, and camera.","history_selection_status":"Already executed. Only compare editing requirements; historical appearance words are not observed facts.","original_user_request":"Using the provided source video, apply the following edit: Please replace the person in the video with the person shown in the reference photo. Only use the reference photo to determine the target person's facial identity and skin tone. Apply that skin tone consistently to the face and body, while retaining the current hairstyle, hair color, clothing, expression, action, scene, and camera.","output_video_card":{"observed":{"action":"The character stands on a cobblestone street, turning her body and posing with one hand on her hip and the other raised near her head.","camera":"A static, medium-full shot that captures the character from head to toe against the street background.","clothing":"A short, white romper with a colorful floral pattern in pink, yellow, and blue, paired with black and white sneakers.","hair_color":"Deep maroon or burgundy.","hairstyle":"Hair is pulled up into a high bun with loose bangs framing the face.","identity":"A 3D-rendered female character with a slim build and brown skin.","scene":"A European-style cobblestone street lined with stone buildings, black lampposts, and a hanging Union Jack flag."},"uncertain":[]}}

arguments.observed_change: The character's face and body now show a darker brown skin tone compared with the lighter source character. The maroon bun, bangs, floral romper, sneakers, street scene, camera framing, and posing motion remain essentially the same.
arguments.requested_change: Replace the person's facial identity and skin tone with the reference person, applying the darker skin tone consistently to face and body while retaining hairstyle, hair color, clothing, expression, action, scene, and camera.
uncertain: Whether the facial identity specifically matches the reference photo, since the output face is small and mostly shown in profile or at a distance.
